`/workspace/src/circt/fsm_dialect.py` implements the CIRCT `fsm` dialect as four registered operations plus one encoding enum, all built on the existing `HWOp` base so they share the `SignalEnv`/`read_operand` machinery with `hw`, `comb` and `seq`. `FSM_DIALECT = Dialect("fsm", get_default_context())` registers `MachineOp` ("fsm.machine"), `StateOp` ("fsm.state"), `TransitionOp` ("fsm.transition") and `FSMOutputOp` ("fsm.output") at the bottom of the file via the usual `for _op in (...)` idiom. `StateEncoding` (BINARY / ONE_HOT / GRAY) provides `parse`, `encode(index, num_states)` (one-hot `1 << index`, Gray `index ^ (index >> 1)`, with a range check) and `width_for(num_states)` (`num_states` bits for one-hot, `(num_states - 1).bit_length()` otherwise, never below 1). `MachineOp` carries `Trait.SYMBOL | ISOLATED_FROM_ABOVE | GRAPH_REGION`, a graph-region body of states, class-level defaults for `encoding` and `_current_state`, and a `build_parsed` that re-derives the encoding from the `stateEncoding`/`encoding` attribute; it exposes `machine_name`, `sym_name`, `block`, `body`, `ports`/`input_ports`/`output_ports` (delegating to `HWModuleOp.ports.fget` since the parser lists `fsm.machine` in `PORT_LIST_OPS` and hands it the same `port_names`/`port_directions`/`function_type` attributes), `states`, `state_names()`, `find_state(name)` (tolerates a leading `@`), `num_states`, `initial_state` (falls back to the first state), `add_state`, `state_width()`, `encode_state(name)`, and the executable surface `current_state` (property + setter), `reset_state()`, `step(env)`, `run(inputs_per_cycle, reset=True)` and `outputs(env)`, plus a `verify_op` catching a missing symbol, duplicate state names, an undefined initial state and transitions to unknown states. `StateOp` holds transitions followed by an optional `fsm.output` (the output goes last because `Block.verify` requires terminators to end their block) and offers `state_name`, `transitions`, `output_op`, `add_transition(t)` (inserts before the terminator), `body_region()`, `next_state(env)` and `evaluate(env)`; `TransitionOp` stores its target as a `FlatSymbolRefAttr` and reads it back through `target` (checking `target`/`next_state`/`sym_name`, so parsed `fsm.transition @Next` works), with `guard` as a class-level `None` default, `is_always_taken` and `is_enabled(env)`; `FSMOutputOp` is a `TERMINATOR`/`PURE` op whose `evaluate` returns the list of operand values like `hw_dialect.OutputOp`. A module-level `_string_attr(op, *names)` helper reconciles the parser's `sym_name` with hand-built `name`/`target` attributes. Verified by importing the module (the only remaining failure is `circt.firrtl_dialect`, a sibling another agent has not written yet), by hand-building and simulating a three-state machine (guarded transitions, reset, `run` over five cycles, encoding widths, verifier diagnostics), and by round-tripping parsed IR (`fsm.machine @Foo(in %go: i1, out done: i1) attributes {initialState = "A", stateEncoding = "one_hot"}` with nested states/transitions) through `mlir.parser.parse` and `Verifier`.

Exported names (`__all__`): `FSM_DIALECT`, `StateEncoding`, `MachineOp`, `StateOp`, `TransitionOp`, `FSMOutputOp`

Created `/workspace/src/circt/sv_dialect.py` (only file touched). Verified end-to-end: it imports cleanly (the only failure from `importlib.import_module('circt.sv_dialect')` is the still-missing sibling `circt.firrtl_dialect`), every op registers with `SV_DIALECT`, round-trips through the real parser/printer (`sv.reg`, `sv.wire`, `sv.assign`, `sv.if` with a region, `sv.alwaysff {clockEdge = "negedge"}`, `sv.alwayscomb`, `sv.generate`, `sv.interface` inside an `hw.module` all parse into their concrete classes via `build_parsed` and pass `Verifier.verify` with no errors), and all accessors/semantics were exercised with assertions in throwaway scripts that have been deleted.

Design: a `SVOp(HWOp)` base supplies `default_num_results() == 0` plus region plumbing (`region_at`/`block_at`/`ops_at`/`append_to`/`body_region`/`body`/`append`) built on a module-private `_region_of` helper that materialises a region and its entry block on demand — necessary because the parser attaches only the regions it saw, so `sv.if`'s else arm may be absent. `SVRegOp` holds `reg_name`/`current_value`/`initial_value` with `read`/`write` (width-truncating via `HWOp.truncate`)/`reset_state`/`evaluate`; `SVWireOp` holds `wire_name`/`driven_value` with `driver`/`has_driver`/`assign`/`evaluate`, mirroring `hw.WireOp`'s literal-or-operand driver; `AssignOp` exposes `destination`/`source`/`destination_width()` (falls back to the declaring reg/wire when the destination type is an opaque `!hw.inout`) and `apply(env)`/`evaluate(env)`; `IfOp` owns two regions with `then_region`/`else_region`/`then_body`/`else_body`/`has_else`/`append_then`/`append_else`/`condition_value`/`taken_branch`/`taken_body`; `AlwaysCombOp` owns one region, `AlwaysFFOp` adds `clock_edge`/`reset_edge` (canonicalised by `_normalise_edge`, mirrored into `clockEdge`/`resetEdge` string attributes) with real transition detection in `triggers_on(prev, cur)`/`reset_triggers_on(...)` via `_edge_detected`; `InterfaceOp` keeps `(name, type)` pairs with `signal_names`/`has_signal`/`get_signal`/`add_signal` (rebinds rather than mutates so the immutable class-level default is never shared); `GenerateOp` keeps its `label` in an attribute so it survives print/parse. `SVModuleOp` subclasses `HWModuleOp` to reuse the `Port`/`Direction` encoding and `ports`/`input_ports`/`output_ports`/`get_port`/`body`/`block` accessors, adds `body_region`/`append`/`ports_with_direction`, and replaces (rather than duplicates) the signature verification with a `sym_name` check since an `sv.module` body is procedural and not terminated by `hw.output`. Every class with extra instance state (`SVRegOp`, `SVWireOp`, `AlwaysFFOp`, `InterfaceOp`) has both class-level defaults and a `build_parsed` classmethod.

Exported public names (`__all__`): `SV_DIALECT`, `SVOp`, `SVModuleOp`, `SVRegOp`, `SVWireOp`, `AssignOp`, `IfOp`, `AlwaysCombOp`, `AlwaysFFOp`, `InterfaceOp`, `GenerateOp`.
